coordinates.locator: arXiv:0712.3094, section 2 (Detector and Observations); arXiv:1207.6003, section 6.2
coordinates.note: Published to one arcminute (136 deg 47 min E, 31 deg 06 min S, 160 m a.s.l.), about 1.8 km, and converted to decimal degrees; arXiv:1207.6003 gives the same numbers. No fetched source gives the telescope positions more precisely, so this is a site-level point (A23). A 2001 design study lists the site as 136 deg E, 31 deg S at 220 m.
coordinates.quote: operated in Woomera, South Australia (longitude 136◦ 47′ E, latitude 31◦ 06′ S, 160 m a.s.l.)

name: CANGAROO site, Woomera
notes: The CANGAROO-I paper (arXiv:0906.4924) quotes the same position and altitude for the 3.8 m telescope; the Mirzoyan review (arXiv:2406.15037) gives 165 m a.s.l. at a dark site 12 km north of Woomera for the same telescope.

summary.plain: A flat, dark patch of the South Australian outback near the town of Woomera where the CANGAROO gamma-ray telescopes stood between 1992 and 2011.
summary.technical: CANGAROO observing site near Woomera, South Australia (31 deg 06 min S, 136 deg 47 min E, 160 m a.s.l.), hosting the 3.8 m, 7/10 m and four-telescope 10 m CANGAROO-III imaging Cherenkov arrays.
